acceptance_criteria: `pub struct Circle { pub center: Point3, pub axis: Point3, pub radius: f64 }` and `fn circle_of(&self, s: &Self::Shape, sub: SubShape) -> Result<Circle, KernelError>` on `Kernel`, documented with the definitions above. `axis` is a unit vector. `s` is unchanged.
A vertex, a straight or other non-circular edge, a face that isn't cylindrical, and an index out of range are `KernelError::InvalidInput`.

With `--features occt`, tolerance 1e-9 (sub-shapes found by `face_plane`, `sub_shape_bounding_box` or `work_axis_on`, not hard-coded indices; `axis` compared up to sign): 1. Cylinder r 5, h 10: its top circular edge gives center (0,0,10), axis ±Z, radius 5; its bottom edge center (0,0,0); its cylindrical face center (0,0,5), axis ±Z, radius 5. 2. The box above filleted at radius 1 (`Kernel::fillet`): the fillet face gives center (5,4,1), axis ±X, radius 1; its arc edge at x = 0 gives center (0,4,1), axis ±X, radius 1. 3. A box edge, a box face, a box vertex, a sphere's face and an out-of-range index give `InvalidInput`.
Any new shim function catches all C++ exceptions, as the others do; any new `unsafe` is in `swx-kernel::ffi` with a comment.
`cargo fmt --all --check && cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo test --workspace` pass, and CI's `swx-kernel (occt)` job passes.
QA report (FACTORY §6b) posted on the PR.
